Optimal.Notes: A slight bump in texture quality and view distance over MaxBattery for better readability of distant threats, while keeping shadows and foliage low to protect frame rate. Drop back to MaxBattery settings if frame rate consistently falls below 28 fps in the open world.

profiles.Summary: Gray Zone Warfare is a demanding open-world tactical shooter whose minimum GPU requirement (GTX 1080) far exceeds the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class), making smooth play a significant challenge. Expect low frame rates even at minimum settings, and be prepared for potential EAC/online connectivity issues under Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements versus Deck hardware capability. On your first run, check the frame rate in an open outdoor area — if it stays below 25 fps consistently, lower view distance and foliage further, and confirm EAC allows online play under GE-Proton before investing time in the settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render resolution dropped to 960x600 with Deck FSR upscaling to recover clarity; all settings at Low to squeeze out every frame. Even so, the Deck is well below minimum spec — expect dips below 30 fps in dense jungle or busy PvP zones.

KnownIssues: Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) may block online play under Proton — verify connectivity before a long session
No controller support is listed; Steam Input remapping or a community layout will likely be required
Minimum GPU spec (GTX 1080 8 GB) is roughly twice the Deck GPU's capability, so frame drops in open-world areas and firefights are expected
Game is Steam Deck 'Unsupported' — launcher behaviour, shader compilation stutter, and stability may vary between updates

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full TDP and GPU clock to chase the 40 Hz cap; realistically the Deck will hit 40 fps only in lighter indoor or low-density areas, with drops to the low 30s in the open world. Battery life is short — best used docked or near a charger.

Optimal.Notes: A slight resolution bump to 1024x640 with FSR upscaling offers a better image than MaxBattery while keeping most settings at Low; textures are raised to Medium since they are largely VRAM-bound rather than GPU-compute-bound. Option names are estimated from UE5 conventions — confirm in-game on first run.

profiles.Summary: Gray Zone Warfare is a demanding open-world tactical shooter that significantly exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities, with minimum PC specs calling for a GTX 1080 — well above the Deck's GTX 1050 Ti-class RDNA 2 GPU. Expect heavy performance compromises; the game is playable at low settings with FSR upscaling but will struggle to hold a stable 30 fps in dense outdoor areas, and the Unsupported Deck rating reflects real compatibility and performance concerns.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck hardware capability. On first launch, verify that the game starts under GE-Proton, confirm in-game graphics option names, and monitor frame rate in an open outdoor area — switch to MaxBattery and lower View Distance further if fps is consistently below 25.

MaxBattery.Notes: Renders at 960x600 and upscales via FSR to ease GPU load; even so, expect dips below 30 fps in large open areas. GPU clock is manually capped to reduce heat and extend battery life. Option names are estimated based on Unreal Engine 5 conventions — verify them in-game.

KnownIssues: Steam Deck is officially 'Unsupported' — the game may not launch or may require workarounds via Proton Experimental or GE-Proton.
Game requires AVX2 CPU instructions; Deck's Zen 2 CPU supports AVX2 but this should be verified on first launch.
As an online-only MMO/PvE shooter, a stable internet connection is required — Wi-Fi latency on Deck may affect gameplay quality.
Heavy CPU and GPU load in open-world areas can cause significant frame drops below 30 fps even at minimum settings.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 1280x800 native render at max TDP extracts every bit of Deck performance, but this game is GPU-limited well beyond the Deck's class — a stable 30 fps is not guaranteed and dips into the low 20s are likely in dense jungle or combat. Reduce View Distance or drop back to the Optimal profile if frame rate is unacceptable.
